nodes.title: Inputs
widgets_values:
## Inputs

Everything here is optional.

### Prompt

Enter a positive prompt and negative prompt.

Supplying an **LTX API key** encodes the prompt through the API
instead of locally, which saves memory. The workflow switches over on its own
whenever a key is present - there is nothing to un-bypass.

See the [prompting guide](https://docs.ltx.io/open-source-model/usage-guides/prompting-guide).


### Source video

The source video is the subject of the edit. Its frames are resized and handed
straight to the IC-LoRA as guide frames.

Its width, height, length and frame rate drive the whole generation, and its audio
track is carried through so the result keeps the original sound. The
**IC-LoRA** is loaded in **Load Models**, the guide frames are injected in
**Preprocess**, then cropped out during sampling.

### Reference image (look still)

The reference image supplies appearance — texture, materials, lighting, palette — while the layout video supplies camera motion and layout. It is added with Add Image IC-LoRA Guide.

It is not image-to-video conditioning. The still is VAE-encoded on its own as a single latent frame and appended to the sequence as clean IC-LoRA reference tokens, in the same way the clay video reference is. It never replaces generated frame 0.

nodes.title: Decode
widgets_values:
## Decode

Make sure to adjust the number of tiles and overlap to fit your hardware.
(fewer tiles will result in faster execution, but will require more memory).

### Recommended settings

| node settings (pixels)                     | resolved latent geometry        |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- |
| `512 / 64 / 128 / 32`                      | 16x16, ov 2 - 16f ov 4 |
| `768 / 192 / 128 / 32`                     | 24x24, ov 6 - 16f ov 4 |
| `1024 / 256 / 128 / 48`                    | 32x32, ov 8 - 16f, ov 6         |
| `1536 / 384 / 192 / 48`                    | 48x48, ov 12 - 24f, ov 6        |
| `768 / 192 / spatial-only`                 | 24x24, ov 6 - no temporal split |

nodes.title: Preprocess
widgets_values:
### Preprocess

Builds the video latent at the resized source size and length, conditions on the optional start image, sets the conditioning frame rate from the source fps, and injects the source guide frames via the IC-LoRA (LTXAddVideoICLoRAGuide, frame_idx = 0) so the generated clip follows the source camera and layout.

The reference still uses the same node, with frame_idx = -1 (see above). Video reference or single still is just how many frames you hand it; frame_idx is the RoPE position in pixel frames and is the only thing that distinguishes them.

The model only accepts frame counts of the form 8k+1, so both the canvas and the guide are rounded down to the nearest valid length. The output is therefore the source length rounded down, and the last few source frames may be dropped. Canvas and guide use the same rule, so they always agree.

Audio is a silent latent (LTXVEmptyLatentAudio) — this flow generates no audio, and the source clip needs no audio track.

Each stage crops its own guides after sampling (LTXVCropGuides) so only the generated video is decoded. The crop must also run before any resolution change: guide positions are recorded in pixel coordinates, and an upscaled latent no longer matches them.

Notes

- The start image is genuine I2V and does replace generated frame 0. Do not point it at the reference still — the still is already conditioned at RoPE −1, and doing both makes one image fight itself for frame 0.
- A negative frame_idx is a position before the clip, not an index counted back from its end. Only non-negative values are snapped to 1 mod 8.

nodes.title: Upscale - stage 2
widgets_values:
## Upscale and re-sample (stage 2)

Upsamples the stage-1 latent 2x and runs a short second denoise at full resolution with the same model, IC-LoRA and references. It continues the sigma schedule where stage 1 stopped rather than restarting, so it refines detail instead of regenerating.

Guides do not survive a resolution change: their positions are pixel coordinates recorded against the latent they were added to. So stage 1 crops its guides before handing the latent on, and stage 2 re-encodes the references at the new size and adds them again — video reference at frame_idx = 0, reference still at frame_idx = -1. It then crops its own guides so only the generated video is decoded.

Stage 2 builds conditioning from the encoded prompt, not from stage 1's conditioning output. That output still carries guide positions recorded at the smaller resolution, and mixing the two resolutions is rejected by the model.

nodes.title: OmniCam layout authoring - record a graybox playblast
OmniCam - generic video passthrough (Layout to Render test)
Bundled OmniCam playblast - fallback until you record

widgets_values:
## OmniCam Layout to Render

This uses External / Generic Reference Video, not LTX Motion Track. Motion layers are not needed.

Upload examples/assets/ltx-layout/omnicam_layout_guide.webm and omnicam_layout_look.png into the corresponding loaders for the tested starter. The guide was recorded in OmniCam; its saved authoring state was unavailable, so the Director contains a new approximate blockout, not a recovered camera solve.

To author your own shot, edit the graybox scene and Record Playblast in the Director. Its new recording takes priority over the fallback loader. Generate an art-directed image from the first layout frame and replace Look Still. Do not use the raw proxy as Look Still.

This starter takes the first 25 guide frames, renders 640x320, then upscales to 1280x640. Increase ImageFromBatch length inside Source Video to use more of your playblast. Prefer 24fps; use 8n+1 frames and dimensions divisible by 64.

## Source video

Everything the generation is sized and timed by comes from here. The frames are
resized to the generation resolution and handed to the IC-LoRA as guide frames,
and the width, height, length and frame rate are all read off this video.

The audio track is passed through too, so the result keeps the original sound.
